pr.title: fix(design-system): one petrol scale, with a general guard against @theme and :root diverging (ugcportal-uo15)

round1Body:
<!-- ugcportal-review-round: 1 -->
Review round 1 (chain approx — self-asserted, reviewer is the PR author; no prior round markers exist, bootstrap probe found only the unrelated K4 visual-check comment, not a prior review round, so B=0), head 5647f4a0e34884a89766bf6f32930b91992a667e. CI green on both jobs, no sensitive paths touched, base/mergeable OK.

Gates run: `npm run lint && npm test && npm run build && npm run typecheck` in a throwaway worktree at the PR head (`/tmp/pr193-review`, `npm install` + `prisma generate` first). All four clean. Tests: 204 files / 4564 tests — matches the PR's claim exactly (main baseline is 204/4553, so +11 tests/0 new files, consistent with "no test files added or removed").

**K3 guard generality — verified, not just read.** Built a throwaway probe test (not part of this PR) feeding `findColorScaleNameCollisions` a brand-new colliding pair under names never mentioned anywhere in this codebase: `--color-coral-300`/`--coral-300` (different hex) → caught; `--color-slate-deep`/`--slate-deep` (different hex, the non-numeric step) → caught; `--color-mint-150`/`--mint-150` (same hex) → correctly not flagged. The guard is genuinely written to the invariant, not to "petrol" by name.

**Rename sweep — one real finding.** Grepped the whole repo for `petrol-{300,400,600,700,800,900,950,deep}` outside historical/explicitly-labelled-as-before comments and test fixtures that deliberately reference the non-compiling `text-petrol-900` shape. No live, rendered call site was missed — every real source usage (`globals.css`, `button.tsx`, `upload-form.tsx`, `upload-queue-list.tsx`) is correctly updated to `fjord-*`.

One place was not caught, and it's new text this PR itself added:

- **`src/lib/design/contrast.ts`, new `SCALE_STEP_PROPERTY` doc comment** (part of the new `findColorScaleNameCollisions` export this PR adds): "the literal `deep` (this app's one non-numeric step, `` --color-petrol-deep ``/`` --color-fjord-deep ``)". `--color-petrol-deep` does not exist anywhere in the codebase after this PR's own rename — `globals.css` only declares `--color-fjord-deep` now, and this PR's own new test two describe-blocks above ("no longer has a --color-petrol-* entry at the steps this bead renamed away", which explicitly includes `"deep"` in its step list) asserts exactly that. The doc comment contradicts a test added in the same diff. **Severity: low** (pure comment/description accuracy — not reachable by a user, doesn't affect Tailwind emission since it's a `--color-` reference inside a JSDoc block, not a bare utility string). **Confidence: CONFIRMED** — verified directly by grep against the worktree at this PR's head commit, and the contradiction is internal to this same diff.

Secondary, non-blocking observation (flagging rather than treating as a finding against this PR): `eslint.config.mjs`'s hardcoded-hex-colour lint message still gives `text-petrol-600` as its example of "a theme color token... defined in src/app/globals.css" — pre-existing text, untouched by this diff, and `text-petrol-600` never compiled to a real Tailwind utility either before or after this PR (petrol-600..950 live outside `@theme` on purpose, same as the analogous `ugcportal-hiae` pre-existing-comment case this PR correctly left alone). Worth a follow-up low-priority bead for hygiene, not something I'm treating as introduced by this PR.

**Required family sweep (review-standards section 2), per angle:**
1. *Comment claims a guarantee the code doesn't make* — found (the `--color-petrol-deep` doc comment above).
2. *Check compares the wrong two things* — none found; `findColorScaleNameCollisions` resolves both sides of a candidate pair through the identical `resolveToken`/`parseColor`/`toHex` path, symmetrically.
3. *Assertion that cannot fail* — none found; the K3 fixture-mutation tests are real (verified independently with new scale names above, not just by reading), and the implementer's own hand-revert proof (5 tests red) is consistent with that.
4. *Sibling-omission* — none found in rendered/compiled code (every real call site updated); the `eslint.config.mjs` item above is the closest candidate but is pre-existing, non-functional, and not introduced by this diff, so not counted as a sibling the rename was obligated to catch.

**Other items from the brief:**
- K4: treated as met per the sanctioned comment already on this PR; not re-run.
- `ugcportal-hiae`: confirmed genuinely pre-existing — the stale "both var(--color-petrol-400)" claim in `contrast.test.ts` is unmodified context in this diff (only the new `NOTE (ugcportal-uo15)` line pointing at the bead was added). Correctly left alone under scope freeze.
- `--color-petrol-50` not renamed: reviewed as principled, not half-migrated — it has no hex counterpart in `docs/design/tokens.css` at any point, so K3's invariant (a `--color-<name>-<step>`/`--<name>-<step>` pair resolving differently) structurally cannot apply to it.
- claims-audit: ran it myself (`ABSOLUTE 81, MEASUREMENT 18, TEMPORAL 21, HISTORY 31, REFERENCE 0`, matching the PR body exactly). Spot-checked several MEASUREMENT lines (`5.57:1` in `upload-queue-list.tsx`, `4.66:1` in `contrast.ts`) — both are unmodified pre-existing values carried through the rename untouched, and the underlying token value is unchanged (only renamed), so they remain accurate.

Blocking under round 1's strict gate (any finding, any severity) on the one CONFIRMED low-severity finding above. Please fix the `--color-petrol-deep` doc comment (either drop the stale example or correct it to only reference `--color-fjord-deep`, consistent with this PR's own "no longer has a --color-petrol-* entry at the steps this bead renamed away" test).
